title: The Country
note: This chapter tells of the country, which the ruler and minister carry forward, and which the other parts of the state, such as the fortress, can’t do without.

couplets.plain: A country is where unfailing harvests, worthy people and the rich who never decline all come together.
couplets.pm: A country is where three live together. Farmers whose harvests never fall short mean no one is poor. The righteous, ascetics, sages and the like, mean it doesn’t perish. The rich, merchants who bring rare goods by ship and by land, supply wealth to the ruler and the people.

links.quote: unfailing harvests, worthy people and the rich who never decline
links.reason: Measures a land by harvests that never fail and by the worthy and the rich who settle there.

couplets.plain: A country is a land desired for its great wealth, which yields abundantly because ruin rarely touches it.
couplets.pm: A country is desired even by other lands for its boundless wealth and yields abundantly, free from ruin. Ruin comes from too much rain, no rain, rats, locusts, parrots and a hostile ruler close by. The ruler’s righteousness keeps away the first five, and his valour the last.

links.reason: Great wealth makes it desired, and freedom from ruin keeps its fields yielding.

couplets.plain: A country bears every burden that falls on it at once, and still gives its ruler his whole tax.
couplets.pm: When all the burdens other lands have carried come on a country at once, it takes them in, and on top of that freely pays its ruler all his dues. The burdens are people and herds of cattle and buffalo fleeing invasion, a crooked sceptre or want of food in their own lands. It lets them live as well as they did at home.

links.quote: bears every burden that falls on it at once
links.reason: Its greatness shows when every burden falls at once and it still holds up.

links.quote: gives its ruler his whole tax
links.reason: The country here is its people, who bear the load and still pay the ruler in full.

couplets.plain: A country runs free of deep hunger, endless sickness and destroying enemies.
couplets.pm: A country goes on happily without great hunger, unending sickness or enemies from outside. Hunger stays away because it has farmers and abundant yields. Sickness stays away because its winds, cold, heat and food do no harm. Enemies stay away because of the ruler’s strength, the standing army, forests and fortresses.

links.quote: free of deep hunger, endless sickness and destroying enemies
links.reason: Names three things a country is spared: deep hunger, endless sickness and destroying enemies.

couplets.plain: A country has no rival factions, no ruinous enemies within and no murderous rebels who harry the ruler.
couplets.pm: A country has no factions gathered against each other, bound by caste or god. It has no enemies within who lay it waste: highwaymen, thieves, slanderers, and boars, tigers and bears. It has no killers who harry the ruler when the chance comes. A country is where ruler and people drive these out.

links.reason: Greatness here is unity: no rival factions and no murderous rebels loose inside the realm.
Counts enemies inside the country among what would ruin it.

couplets.plain: The land that knows no ruin, and whose riches hold even when it is ruined, is called the first of countries.
couplets.pm: The learned call the first of all countries the one that knows no ruin from enemies, and whose riches don’t fall even on the rare day it is ruined. The ruler’s strength, worship of the gods and righteous acts keep ruin away. Its riches, from mines, fields and groves, don’t fall because they come by nature or have been stored up.

links.quote: knows no ruin, and whose riches hold even when it is ruined
links.reason: Crowns the land that escapes ruin and whose riches hold even if ruin comes.

couplets.plain: The two waters, a well-placed hill, running water and a strong fortress are the limbs of a country.
couplets.pm: Water below and above the ground, a well-placed hill, the water that comes from it and a walled city that can’t fall are the limbs of a country. The waters are wells, tanks and rivers, so there is plenty even if the sky fails. The hill stands to one side, gives its own riches, and pours out in summer what it drank in the rains.

links.quote: are the limbs of a country
links.reason: Names the limbs of a country: its waters, its hill and its strong fortress.

links.remove: Rainwater is the old English. The Tamil says water, and he reads it as wells, tanks and rivers that last when the sky fails.

links.reason: Closes the list of a country’s limbs with a strong fortress.

couplets.plain: They say five things are a country’s ornament: freedom from sickness, wealth, harvest, happiness and safety.
couplets.pm: The learned say these five adorn a country: no sickness, wealth, yield, happiness and protection. Good land keeps sickness away. Happiness comes from festivals, sacrifices, worthy people, things to enjoy and good land and water. Protection is the ruler’s, the people’s and the fortress’s. This beauty makes people of other lands long for it and forget their own.

links.quote: five things are a country’s ornament
links.reason: Gives five marks of a fine country, from health and wealth to happiness and safety.
Wealth is one of the five things named.
A country wears its health, plenty and safety as an ornament.

couplets.plain: A country is a land whose riches come without seeking. Land that gives riches only when sought is no country.
couplets.pm: The learned call a country the land whose wealth comes to the people living there without their toiling after it. So lands that give wealth only to those who seek and toil are not countries. Seeking, in both lines, means toil.

links.reason: Withholds the name of country from land that gives riches only when they are sought.

couplets.plain: Even with all of this, a country is of no use if it isn’t well matched with its ruler.
couplets.pm: A country without accord with its ruler is of no use, even if it is full of all the qualities named above. Accord means the people have loving-kindness for him and he has compassion for them. Without these no one stays to live there, so all the rest is useless.

links.quote: isn’t well matched with its ruler
links.reason: Makes accord with the ruler the last test: without it, all a country’s gifts are of no use.

ideaLinks.quote: a strong fortress are the limbs of a country
ideaLinks.reason: A strong fortress is named among the limbs of a country.

ideaLinks.remove: Rainwater is the old English. The Tamil says water, and he reads it as wells, tanks and rivers that last when the sky fails.

ideaLinks.quote: a country is of no use if it isn’t well matched with its ruler
ideaLinks.reason: All of a country’s gifts come to nothing unless it is well matched with its ruler.
